- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or rising slowly, adjust upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is neutral or bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 2–5% buffer to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤0.00) and price is trending up, model often fails to reverse; force a downward correction by 2–5% in next 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >5% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent 15-day trend, not 30-day trend.  
- If recent auction events are frequent (≥3/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to underestimate price volatility; increase forecast variance by 1–2% for next 7 days.
